This keeps settings safe from little fingers.
Short tips for parents, teachers and therapists using Eraka with a child.
Tap the pictures yourself while you talk – \"Let\'s GO to the PARK\". Children learn to use the board by watching you use it, the same way they learn speech by hearing it.
Make the phone or tablet available all day – at meals, in the car, at play – not only during \"practice time\". Words are learnt where they are needed.
Words like MORE, STOP, GO, WANT, HELP, LIKE and NOT work in many situations. Use them often before adding lots of nouns.
After you ask something, pause and count slowly to ten in your head. Give the child time to find the picture.
Respond to every attempt, even if it seems random. If the child taps STOP by accident, stop and see what happens – it teaches that the words have power.
Using pictures does not stop speech from developing. Never take the device away as a punishment – it is the child\'s voice.
Tap pictures to add them to the sentence strip, then press the yellow Speak button. Delete removes the last picture; hold it to clear everything.
Open the menu and choose \"Where are we?\" – School, Park, Shop… Eraka will then suggest words that fit. No GPS or internet is used.
Tap Voice and speak: Eraka listens on the phone itself and turns your words into pictures. Recordings never leave the device.
Settings, the profile, the progress report and signing out ask a small maths question first, so the child can explore freely without changing things by accident.

Eraka is a free picture-based communication (AAC) app. It helps children who don\'t speak, or speak only a little – including autistic children – say what they want, need and feel by tapping pictures that Eraka speaks out loud. It was designed for children and families in Namibia and works without internet.
Works offline: the word board, speech and voice recognition all run on this phone. Voice recordings never leave the device.
Saved on this phone: the child\'s first name, birthday, communication level, interests, avatar or photo, and the sentences they build (used for word suggestions and the progress report).

When online, a backup of the profile, board and sentences is kept in the Google account used to sign in (Google Firebase), so it can be restored on a new phone. Photos you add are never uploaded: they stay on this phone.
No location tracking: places are chosen by hand in \"Where are we?\".
Anonymous usage statistics (for example which buttons are used) help us improve Eraka.
To remove data: sign out and uninstall Eraka to clear this phone. To delete the online backup, email us and we will remove it.
Questions, ideas or problems? We\'d love to hear from you.
Eraka is based on the open-source OTTAA project and is shared under the GNU GPL v3 licence.

Pictographic symbols: the property of the Government of Aragón, created by Sergio Palao for ARASAAC (https://arasaac.org), distributed under a Creative Commons licence (BY-NC-SA). Some English labels were corrected for Eraka. Some pictures are photographs and drawings added for Eraka. Avatars: Avataaars by Pablo Stanley (avataaars.com), free for personal and commercial use, generated with DiceBear.
Also uses: whisper.cpp (OpenAI Whisper model, MIT licence) for speech recognition and SimpleNLG (Mozilla Public Licence 2.0) for sentence grammar.

Voices installed on this phone that work without internet.

No male voice is installed on this phone yet. To add one: Android Settings → Text-to-speech output → Google (settings icon) → Install voice data → English (United Kingdom) → choose a voice marked as male and download it. Then come back to this page.
For an accent closer to Namibian English, install a British English voice: phone Settings → Text-to-speech → Google → Install voice data → English (United Kingdom). Eraka will then use it.
No extra offline voices found. You can add more in the phone\'s Settings → Text-to-speech.
